methodology:
MP Evans is a UK-listed Indonesian palm oil pure-play with the unusual structure of USD reporting + GBp listing — making it a dual-currency comp row. The Properties table values are in USD (the reporting currency); the listed GBp price gets converted to USD for market-cap calculations.

The portfolio of 70,900 planted hectares (~175K acres) is split across 5 Indonesian provinces. The 4-row aggregation reflects MP Evans' geographic clusters: North Sumatra (most mature cluster, multiple mills), South Sumatra (Musi Rawas concession with 2024-commissioned mill), East Kalimantan (Bumi Mas + ABK expansion), and Aceh + Bangka-Belitung (smaller residual).

Indonesian palm oil land valuation depends heavily on:
- Plantation maturity (immature 0-3 years has minimal harvestable value; 4-25 year mature is peak; replant cycle 25-30 years)
- Mill access (within 30-40km of a CPO mill commands premium for fresh fruit bunch transport economics)
- Concession term remaining (HGU rights 30 years renewable, time-to-renewal matters)
- 2024-25 CPO prices ($800-900/tonne range) supportive of higher land values

The aggregate ~$5K USD/acre weighted average reflects these factors. Concrete per-region anchors come from GAPKI (Indonesian palm oil association) land transaction reports and broker comps for Sumatra/Kalimantan, all 2024-2025 dated.

Land book of $300M is a rough estimate — MP Evans' GAAP balance sheet bundles plantation asset (biological asset under IAS 41 fair value) with land. Their reported gross profit jumped 49% in 2024 driven by CPO prices, reflected in plantation asset revaluations. Refining the land-vs-plantation-asset split would tighten the book number.
